q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, a member of Parliament who is unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English may address the House in his mother tongue with the permission of the presiding officer.
2. Under Article 210 of the Constitution, no such facility of addressing the House in the mother tongue is available to a member of a State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Article 120 permits mother-tongue address with the presiding officer permission. A similar facility does exist under Article 210 for State Legislatures, so statement 2 is false.

q: A Central Government office receives a letter written in Hindi from a member of the public. The dealing assistant, citing heavy workload, replies to it in English and records that the language of reply is discretionary. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The reply is not in order; a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi
options.B: The reply is in order; workload is a valid ground for replying in English
options.C: The reply should have been issued in the regional language of the office
options.D: The reply is in order if a copy is endorsed to the Hindi Cell

e: Under the Official Language Rules a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi. Heavy workload does not make an English reply permissible, as the language of reply is not discretionary.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Ministry of Education.
2. The Central Hindi Directorate also functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology and the Central Hindi Directorate both function under the Ministry of Education, not the Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: A Central Government office proposes to print and publish a departmental manual in English only, on the ground that the subject is technical. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The proposal is in order for technical manuals
options.B: Manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature are required to be printed and published in diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.C: The manual should be published in Hindi only
options.D: The manual should be published in the regional language only

e: Under Rule 11 manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature must be printed and published in diglot form, in Hindi and English, even where the subject is technical.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.
2. The members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by its members from amongst themselves, and members are elected by both Houses by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.

q: Which of the following pairings of the award of the Department of Official Language with its field is correct?

options.A: Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar — Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy
options.B: Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar — original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects
options.C: Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar — the best Zonal Railway in implementing the Official Language Policy
options.D: Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar — the best Division located in Region 'C'

e: Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is awarded to Ministries, Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy, which is the correct pairing.

q: In a High Court where the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees and orders has been authorised under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a litigant objects that a judgment delivered in Hindi was not accompanied by any English version. Under the Act, the correct position is:

options.A: The judgment is complete in itself and needs no accompaniment
options.B: The judgment must be accompanied by a summary in the regional language
options.C: The judgment must be accompanied by a certificate of the Registrar of the High Court
options.D: Every such judgment, decree or order shall be accompanied by a translation thereof in the English language issued under the authority of the High Court

e: Under Section 7, every judgment, decree or order passed in Hindi by such a High Court must be accompanied by an English translation issued under the authority of the High Court.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. In making its recommendations, the Commission shall have due regard to the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under Article 344 the Commission has a Chairman and members representing Eighth Schedule languages, and it must have due regard to just claims of non-Hindi speaking areas in public services.

q: A citizen submits a representation for the redress of a grievance to a Central Government authority in a language which is in use in the State in which he resides, but which is neither Hindi nor English. The receiving office proposes to return it as not being in an official language. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, the correct position is:

options.A: The representation must be returned; only Hindi is admissible
options.B: The representation must be returned; only English is admissible
options.C: The representation is admissible only if accompanied by a Hindi translation paid for by the citizen
options.D: The representation is admissible; every person is entitled to submit a representation in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be

e: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a grievance representation in any language used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be, so it cannot be returned merely for not being in Hindi or English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.
2. The Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except Tamil Nadu, whereas the Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India.

q: With a view to ensuring that every document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 leaves the office in both Hindi and English, an office marks its despatch section as the point through which every such document must pass before issue. In Rajbhasha terminology, such a marked point is known as a:

options.D: Vigilance Points

e: A marked point such as the despatch section, through which Section 3(3) documents must pass to ensure bilingual issue, is known in Rajbhasha terminology as a Check Point.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year 2006.
2. The first World Hindi Conference was held at Nagpur in January 1975 and was inaugurated by Smt. Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: World Hindi Day on 10 January was first observed in 2006, and the first World Hindi Conference was held at Nagpur in January 1975 and inaugurated by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

q: A Ministry of the Central Government issues a communication in English to its attached office situated in Region 'A', without any Hindi version, and the attached office objects. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The objection is not valid; inter-office communications may always be in English alone
options.B: The objection is not valid; the rule applies only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.C: The objection is valid only if the attached office is a notified office
options.D: If a communication to an office in Region 'A' is issued in English, it must be accompanied by its Hindi translation

e: Under the Official Language Rules, if a communication to an office in Region A is issued in English, it must be accompanied by its Hindi translation, so the attached office objection is valid.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Hindi translation of a Central Act, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. A Hindi translation of an Act passed by a State Legislature in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi under Section 6 of the Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Section 5 covers Central Acts under the President authority. For State Acts, Section 6 publication is under the Governor authority, not the President, so statement 2 is false.

q: During an inspection, an inspecting officer insists that every noting recorded in Hindi on a file must invariably be accompanied by an English translation prepared by the noting employee himself. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The employee must furnish the translation as directed
options.B: The employee cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting in the other language
options.C: The translation must be furnished only if the employee is a gazetted officer
options.D: The translation must be prepared by the employee at his own cost through the Hindi Translator

e: Under Rule 8 an employee noting in Hindi or English cannot be required to furnish a translation of his own noting in the other language, so the inspecting officer direction is not in order.

q: Which of the following pairings of the committee with its chairman is correct?

options.A: Official Language Implementation Committee of an office — the Hindi Translator of the office
options.B: Town Official Language Implementation Committee — the District Magistrate of the district
options.C: Town Official Language Implementation Committee — the senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose
options.D: Official Language Implementation Committee of an office — the nominee of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer, the head of office, in the town nominated for the purpose, which is the correct pairing.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 349 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, no Bill or amendment relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts could be introduced in either House of Parliament without the previous sanction of the President.
2. Article 349 lays down a special procedure for the enactment of certain laws relating to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 349 prescribes a special procedure, requiring previous sanction of the President during the first fifteen years, for Bills relating to language of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

q: A contractor engaged for station renovation paints the name board of a railway station with the languages arranged in the order Hindi, English and the regional language. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the correct position is:

options.B: The order should be English, Hindi and the regional language
options.C: The order should be Hindi, the regional language and English
options.D: The boards are required to be displayed in the order: regional language, Hindi, English

e: Railway station name boards are displayed in the order regional language, Hindi and English, so the contractor order of Hindi, English and regional language is incorrect.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of the Ministry.
2. The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister of Railways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of that Ministry, and the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister of Railways.

q: A section of a Central Government office prepares a proposal addressed to the embassy of a foreign country located in India in bilingual form, on the analogy of Section 3(3) documents. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, correspondence with a foreign embassy is conducted in:

options.C: Both Hindi and English, as in the case of Section 3(3) documents
options.D: The official language of the foreign country concerned

e: Correspondence with a foreign embassy in India is conducted in English. The bilingual rule for Section 3(3) documents does not make such embassy correspondence bilingual.

q: The President issues a direction to a State Government requiring it to secure adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education for children belonging to a linguistic minority group. The provision of the Constitution under which such a direction may be issued is:

options.D: Article 351

e: Article 350A empowers the President to issue directions to a State to secure adequate facilities for mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for children of linguistic minority groups.

q: Which of the following pairings of the course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with its description is correct?

options.A: Prabodh — the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff
options.B: Pragya — the course intended for beginners who possess no knowledge of Hindi
options.C: Parangat — the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work
options.D: Praveen — the course prescribed beyond Pragya for advanced proficiency

e: Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work, which is the correct pairing given.

q: An office is found to have inflated the figure of its Hindi correspondence in its Quarterly Progress Report by including letters which were first drafted in English and only thereafter translated into Hindi before issue. With reference to the method of counting Hindi correspondence, the correct position is:

options.A: The letters are correctly counted, translation being equivalent to original Hindi drafting
options.B: The letters are correctly counted if signed by an officer who knows Hindi
options.C: The letters are correctly counted if addressed to offices in Region 'A'
options.D: The letters are not to be counted as Hindi correspondence; only letters originally written and issued in Hindi are counted

e: Only letters originally written and issued in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence for progress reporting. Letters drafted in English and later translated into Hindi are not counted as Hindi correspondence.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau was set up in the year 1971.
2. Besides translation of codes, manuals and other non-statutory material, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Central Translation Bureau was set up in 1971, and besides translating codes, manuals and non-statutory material it also conducts translation training for translators of Central offices.

q: A proposal to redesign the website of a Central Government office in English only is put up on the ground that websites are outside the Official Language Policy. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct; websites are exempt
options.B: The website is required to be maintained in Hindi and English (bilingual form)
options.C: The website should be maintained in Hindi only
options.D: The website should be maintained in the regional language only

e: Websites are covered by the official language policy and a Central Government office website is required to be maintained in bilingual form, in Hindi and English, not in English only.

q: Under Article 351 of the Constitution, it is the duty of the Union to develop Hindi so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India. For its vocabulary, Hindi shall draw:

options.A: Primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages
options.D: Only from the regional languages

e: Article 351 directs that Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, while assimilating forms and expressions of Hindustani and other Eighth Schedule languages.

q: Which of the following pairings of the body with its chairman is correct?

options.A: Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) — the Prime Minister
options.B: Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) — the Union Home Minister
options.C: Central Official Language Implementation Committee — the Prime Minister
options.D: Central Official Language Implementation Committee — the Cabinet Secretary

e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the Central Hindi Committee, is chaired by the Prime Minister, which is the correct body and chairman pairing given.

q: At a railway station, announcements for the guidance of passengers are made only in Hindi and English, and the station staff contend that two languages are sufficient. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct; two languages are sufficient
options.B: Announcements should be made in Hindi only
options.C: Announcements should be made in the regional language only
options.D: Announcements are made in three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Announcements for passengers at railway stations are made in three languages, the regional language, Hindi and English, so Hindi and English alone are not sufficient.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992.
2. The Sindhi language was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992. Sindhi was added earlier, in 1967, not by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003.

q: A Central Government office executes an agreement with a contractor in English only, and the dealing clerk contends that agreements are internal documents outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct; agreements are not covered
options.B: The agreement should have been executed in Hindi only
options.C: The agreement should have been executed in the regional language only
options.D: An agreement is required to be executed in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3)

e: Contracts and agreements executed by or on behalf of the Central Government are covered by Section 3(3) and must be executed in both Hindi and English, so an English-only agreement is not in order.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution is designated as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
2. The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Special Officer under Article 350B is designated the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, and his headquarters is at Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad.

q: An employee claims to possess working knowledge of Hindi solely on the basis of his own written declaration, though he has not passed the Pragya examination, and the head of office refuses to recognise the claim. Under the Official Language Rules, the correct position is:

options.A: The declaration has no value; only a pass in Pragya counts
options.B: The employee shall also be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi on such declaration
options.C: The employee must first complete five years of service in Region 'A'
options.D: The declaration is valid only if countersigned by the Hindi Officer

e: Under Rule 10 an employee who declares himself in the prescribed form to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi is also deemed to have acquired such knowledge, even without passing Pragya.

q: Which of the following pairings of the event with its year is correct?

options.A: Report of the first Official Language Commission submitted to the President — 1960
options.B: Presidential Order on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission — 1956
options.C: Constitution of the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language — 1955
options.D: Report of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) submitted to the President — 1956

e: The first Official Language Commission, the Kher Commission, submitted its report to the President in 1956; the Presidential Order followed in 1960, so the 1956 pairing is the correct one.

q: In a State where the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, has authorised the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court under Article 348(2) of the Constitution, a party contends that the authorisation also covers the judgments of the Court. The authorisation does NOT extend to:

options.A: Any judgment, decree or order passed or made by the High Court
options.B: The arguments of the advocates in the Court
options.C: The pleadings filed in the Court
options.D: The day-to-day proceedings of the Court

e: The proviso to Article 348(2) expressly excludes judgments, decrees and orders of the High Court from a Governor authorisation for use of Hindi or the State official language in court proceedings.

q: During Hindi Pakhwada, a Central Government office proposes to hold only a formal inaugural function on the first day and no other programme. In accordance with the practice under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is:

options.A: The proposal is complete; only an inaugural function is prescribed
options.B: During Hindi Pakhwada, offices normally organise Hindi essay, noting-and-drafting, elocution and Hindi typing competitions, Hindi workshops and related programmes
options.C: During Hindi Pakhwada, a compulsory written Hindi examination for all staff is prescribed
options.D: During Hindi Pakhwada, all non-Hindi knowing staff are to be transferred to Region 'C'

e: During Hindi Pakhwada offices normally organise Hindi essay, noting and drafting, elocution and typing competitions, Hindi workshops and related programmes, not merely an inaugural function.

q: A non-Hindi speaking trainee teacher and a foreign learner both enrol at an institute located at Agra which teaches Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, trains Hindi teachers and conducts research in Hindi. The institute is:

options.D: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi)

e: The institute at Agra teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training Hindi teachers and doing Hindi research is the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, the Central Institute of Hindi.

q: During an inspection of a Central Government office, the rubber stamps in use are found to have been prepared in English only, and the office pleads that stamps are internal stationery. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, the correct position is:

options.A: The stamps are correctly prepared in English only
options.B: The rubber stamps used in the office should be prepared in bilingual form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.C: The stamps should be prepared in the regional language only
options.D: The stamps should be prepared in Hindi only, without exception

e: Rubber stamps in Central Government offices should be prepared in bilingual form, in Hindi and English, so stamps prepared in English only are not in order.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The compromise formula on the official language question, adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September, 1949, is known as the Munshi-Ayyangar formula.
2. The formula is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the compromise formula adopted on 14 September 1949 is the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.

q: A litigant relies upon the Hindi text of the Constitution of India published under the authority of the President as the authoritative text thereof in Hindi. The provision of the Constitution which provides for the authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language is:

options.D: Article 351

e: Article 394A provides for publication, under the President authority, of the Hindi translation of the Constitution, which is deemed the authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

q: A Central Government office prints its letter-heads in English only and contends that letter-heads are not covered by the Official Language Rules, 1976. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct; letter-heads are exempt
options.B: Letter-heads should be printed in Hindi only
options.C: Letter-heads should be printed in the regional language only
options.D: The letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English

e: Letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English under the official language instructions, so English-only letter-heads are not in order.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Complaint". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Sujhav

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Complaint is Shikayat.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Mother Tongue". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Sampark Bhasha

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Mother Tongue is Matribhasha.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Link Language". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Boli

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Link Language is Sampark Bhasha.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dialect". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Shabdavali

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Dialect is Boli, as distinct from Bhasha, which means language.

q: An instructor in a Hindi workshop asks the trainees to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Conference". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Sabha

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Conference is Sammelan.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Competition". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Sakshatkar

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Competition is Pratiyogita, as distinct from Pariksha, which means examination.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Essay". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Nibandh

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Essay is Nibandh.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Fortnight". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Pakshik Patrika

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Fortnight, a period of two weeks, is Pakhwada.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Implementation". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Karyanvayan

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Implementation is Karyanvayan.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Translator". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Anuvadak

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Translator is Anuvadak; Dubhashiya means an interpreter.

q: An accounts clerk preparing a Hindi version of an inspection proforma has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Questionnaire". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Prapatra

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Questionnaire is Prashnavali.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Bilingual". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Bahubhashi

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Bilingual, meaning in two languages, is Dwibhashi.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Award". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Puraskar

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Award is Puraskar.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "National Language". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Rashtrabhasha

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term National Language is Rashtrabhasha, as distinct from Rajbhasha, which means official language.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Interpreter". The correct equivalent is:

options.D: Samvaddata

e: The standard Hindi equivalent used in administrative terminology for the English term Interpreter is Dubhashiya; Anuvadak means a translator.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, it shall be the endeavour of every State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
2. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, the endeavour to provide such facilities rests on the Union Government alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Article 350A makes it the endeavour of every State and local authority to provide mother-tongue instruction facilities at primary stage for linguistic minority children, not of the Union alone.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 120(2) of the Constitution, after the expiration of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English was to cease to be used for the transaction of business in Parliament unless Parliament by law otherwise provided.
2. Under Article 210(2) of the Constitution, after the expiration of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English was to cease to be used for the transaction of business in the Legislature of a State unless the Legislature of the State by law otherwise provided.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Articles 120(2) and 210(2) originally limited English use in Parliament and State Legislatures to fifteen years from commencement, unless the respective legislature by law provided otherwise.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and in every High Court shall be in the English language.
2. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State shall be in the English language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 348(1) provides, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, English for all proceedings in the Supreme Court and High Courts and for authoritative texts of orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of a Central Act, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
2. Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 does not cover Ordinances promulgated by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Section 5 deems a Hindi translation of a Central Act published under the President authority to be the authoritative Hindi text. Section 5 also covers Ordinances, so statement 2 is false.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, the directives on the recommendations of the Official Language Commission are issued by the Chairman of the Commission himself.
2. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, the President may issue directives in accordance with the whole or any part of the report of the Committee of Parliament on the recommendations of the Official Language Commission, after considering that report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: under Article 344 the President may issue directives in accordance with the report of the Committee of Parliament after considering it; the Commission Chairman issues no directives himself.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 345 of the Constitution, the Legislature of a State may by law adopt Hindi as one of the official languages of the State even if Hindi is not in use in that State.
2. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, where two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the language for communication between such States, such communication shall be in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 345 lets a State Legislature adopt any language in use or Hindi as an official language, and the proviso to Article 346 provides Hindi for communication between States that so agree.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and in the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 351 requires Hindi to be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating Hindustani and Eighth Schedule language forms, drawing vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on others.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The service book of a Government employee is a document required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. A press communique issued by a Central Government office is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: a press communique is expressly listed in Section 3(3) and must be bilingual. A service book is not a document listed for bilingual issue under Section 3(3).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rules made by the Central Government are among the documents required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. Bye-laws issued by a Central Government office are among the documents required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: rules and bye-laws issued by the Central Government are expressly listed in Section 3(3) of the Act and must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 394A of the Constitution, the President shall cause to be published under his authority the translation of the Constitution of India in the Hindi language.
2. The translation of the Constitution in Hindi, published under the authority of the President under Article 394A, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 394A requires the President to cause the Hindi translation of the Constitution to be published under his authority, and that translation is deemed the authoritative Hindi text.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar of the Department of Official Language was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.
2. The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded to Ministries and Departments for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar. Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is for original Hindi book writing, not for ministries implementation work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is submitted to the President.
2. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the President shall cause the report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all the State Governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under Section 4 the Committee of Parliament report is submitted to the President, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all State Governments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the expression "Central Government office" includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the expression "Central Government office" includes an office of a State Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: for the Official Language Rules a Central Government office includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government; it does not include a State Government office.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee shall be deemed to possess proficiency in Hindi if he has passed the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme.
2. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee shall be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi if he has passed the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: under Rule 10 passing the Pragya examination gives working knowledge of Hindi. Pragya by itself is not the test of proficiency in Hindi under Rule 9.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi is prepared by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi also fixes targets relating to the purchase of Hindi books for the libraries of Central Government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Annual Programme is prepared by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, and it also fixes targets for purchase of Hindi books for office libraries.

q: A Ministry of the Central Government has to send a communication to its attached office situated in Region 'B'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication may be sent in:

options.A: The regional language of the State only
options.D: Hindi or English

e: Communications between Central Government offices in Region B may be in Hindi or English under the Official Language Rules, so either language may be used for the attached office communication.

q: A State Government office located in Region 'B' has to correspond with a Central Government office on an official matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such correspondence from the State Government office shall ordinarily be in:

options.B: The regional language of the State only
options.D: The regional language, accompanied by its English translation

e: Under the Official Language Rules, correspondence from a State Government office in Region B to a Central Government office shall ordinarily be in Hindi.

q: The Governor of a State, without obtaining the previous consent of the President, authorises the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court of that State under Article 348(2) of the Constitution. The correct position is:

options.A: The authorisation is valid, as the consent of the President is not required
options.B: The authorisation is valid, as the Governor is the head of the State judiciary
options.C: The authorisation is valid only for the subordinate courts of the State
options.D: The authorisation is not valid, as such authorisation can be given only with the previous consent of the President

e: Under Article 348(2) a Governor may authorise Hindi or the State official language in High Court proceedings only with the previous consent of the President, so an authorisation without that consent is invalid.

q: The President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised in that State. An officer records that such recognition, under Article 347 of the Constitution, can be only for the whole of the State and for all purposes. The correct position is:

options.A: The record is correct; recognition can only be for the whole State and for all purposes
options.B: The record is not correct; such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as the President may specify
options.C: The record is correct; recognition can only be for the whole State, though for specified purposes
options.D: The record is not correct; such recognition can be given only by the Governor of the State

e: Under Article 347 the President may direct official recognition of a language for the whole or any part of a State and for such purposes as he specifies, so recognition need not be State-wide or for all purposes.

q: A Central Government office prints the procedural forms used by it in English only, contending that forms are stationery items outside the language rules. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: Manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature are required to be printed and published in diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.B: The contention is correct; forms may be printed in English only
options.C: The forms should be printed in Hindi only
options.D: The forms should be printed in the regional language only

e: Under Rule 11 manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature must be printed and published in diglot form, in Hindi and English, so English-only forms are not in order.

q: A member of Parliament, who is unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English, addresses the House in his mother tongue without seeking the permission of the presiding officer. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, the correct position is:

options.A: The address is in order, as no permission is required for using the mother tongue
options.B: The address is in order, as the member may use any language of the Eighth Schedule
options.C: The address is in order only if the member belongs to a linguistic minority
options.D: The address is not in order, as a member may address the House in his mother tongue only with the permission of the presiding officer of the House

e: Under Article 120 a member unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English may address the House in his mother tongue only with the permission of the presiding officer, so the address without permission is not in order.

q: The Legislature of a State has prescribed a language other than English for the Acts passed by it, and an English translation of one such Act is published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State. A dealing assistant treats that translation as a mere unofficial summary for guidance. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, the correct position is:

options.A: The translation is only a working summary and has no legal status
options.B: The translation shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in the English language
options.C: The translation is valid only within the territory of that State
options.D: The translation requires the approval of Parliament before it can be used

e: Under Article 348(3) an English translation of a State Act published under the Governor authority in the State Gazette is deemed to be the authoritative text of that Act in English.

q: An Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi is translated into Hindi, and the translation is published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the Governor of the State. A dealing assistant treats that translation as a document of no legal value. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: The translation shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.B: The translation is valid only in the States of Region 'A'
options.C: The translation takes effect only after approval by the State Legislature
options.D: The translation is a document of no legal value

e: Under Section 6 a Hindi translation of a State Act published in the State Gazette under the Governor authority is deemed to be the authoritative text of that Act in Hindi.

q: A Central Government office receives a letter written in Hindi from a State Government office. The dealing assistant proposes to reply to it in English, contending that the rule of replying in Hindi applies only to letters received from members of the public. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The proposal is in order, as the contention is correct
options.B: The reply should be sent in the regional language of the State
options.C: The proposal is in order if a copy is endorsed to the Hindi Cell of the office
options.D: The proposal is not in order, as a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi

e: The reply rule is general: a communication received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, whether it came from a member of the public or from a State Government office, so an English reply is not in order.

q: A member of the public submits an application to a Central Government office in English. The dealing assistant returns it, contending that an application to a Central Government office can be submitted in Hindi only. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct; applications can be submitted in Hindi only
options.B: The contention is correct; applications can be submitted in English only after obtaining permission
options.C: The contention is not correct, as a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or English
options.D: The contention is not correct, as the application should have been submitted in the regional language

e: Under the Official Language Rules a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English, so returning an English application is wrong.

q: A Central Government office sends an official communication in Hindi only to a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: The English language shall be used for the purposes of communication between the Union and a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language
options.B: Hindi only shall be used for such communication in every case
options.C: The regional language of that State shall be used for such communication
options.D: Either Hindi or the regional language may be used, at the choice of the sending office

e: Under Section 3(2) the English language shall be used for communication between the Union and a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language.

q: An officer of a Central Government office records that the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution, are submitted by that officer directly to each House of Parliament. The correct position is:

options.A: The record is correct; the reports are submitted directly to Parliament
options.B: The reports are submitted to the Governor of the State concerned
options.C: The reports are submitted to the Union Home Minister, who lays them before Parliament
options.D: The reports are submitted to the President, who shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to the Government of the State concerned

e: Under Article 350B the Special Officer reports to the President, who causes the reports to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to the Government of the State concerned.

q: A Rajbhasha note on railway committees records the Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti as a Member of the Railway Board. The correct position is:

options.A: The record is correct; a Member of the Railway Board chairs the Samiti
options.B: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister of Railways
options.C: The Samiti is chaired by the Chairman, Railway Board
options.D: The Samiti is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language

e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister of Railways, not by a Member of the Railway Board, so the note recording a Board Member as chairman is incorrect.

q: Two Central Government offices, both situated in Region 'C', have to correspond with each other on an official matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such communications may be in:

options.D: Hindi or English

e: Communications between Central Government offices situated in Region C may be in Hindi or English under the Official Language Rules, so either language may be used.

q: A Central Government office issues a press communique in Hindi only, contending that issue in the Official Language of the Union alone is sufficient. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: A press communique is required to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.B: The contention is correct; a press communique may be issued in Hindi only
options.C: A press communique is required to be issued in English only
options.D: A press communique is required to be issued in the regional language only

e: A press communique is expressly listed in Section 3(3) of the Act and must be issued in both Hindi and English, so issue in Hindi only is not sufficient.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' issued 150 letters during a quarter, of which 141 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, as Region 'A' offices have no fixed target
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, its Hindi correspondence being 94 per cent against the prescribed target of 100 per cent
options.C: The office has exactly met the target prescribed for Region 'A'
options.D: The office has met the target, as the target for Region 'A' is only 90 per cent

e: Region A target for Hindi-originating correspondence is 100 per cent. The office achieved 141 of 150, i.e. 94 per cent, so it has fallen short of the prescribed target.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 800 letters during a quarter, of which 736 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has met the target, its Hindi correspondence being 92 per cent against the prescribed target of 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, as Region 'B' offices must achieve 100 per cent Hindi correspondence
options.C: The office has fallen short of the target, its Hindi correspondence being below 95 per cent
options.D: No target applies to the office, Region 'B' being exempt from correspondence targets

e: Region B target is 90 per cent. The office achieved 736 of 800, i.e. 92 per cent, which exceeds 90 per cent, so it has met the target.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 250 letters during a quarter, of which 150 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, as Region 'C' offices must achieve 90 per cent Hindi correspondence
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, its Hindi correspondence being only 60 per cent
options.C: The office has met the target, its Hindi correspondence being 60 per cent against the prescribed target of 55 per cent
options.D: The office has exceeded the target for Region 'A', which alone applies to it

e: Region C target is 55 per cent. The office achieved 150 of 250, i.e. 60 per cent, which exceeds 55 per cent, so it has met the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 300 notes on files, of which 105 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, as the target for noting in Hindi is 50 per cent
options.B: No target for noting in Hindi is prescribed under the Annual Programme
options.C: The office has fallen short, its noting in Hindi being 35 per cent against a target of 55 per cent
options.D: The office has met the target, its noting in Hindi being 35 per cent against the prescribed target of 30 per cent

e: The noting target is 30 per cent. The office wrote 105 of 300 notes in Hindi, i.e. 35 per cent, which exceeds 30 per cent, so it has met the target.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 160 letters, of which 64 were originally written in Hindi and 96 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The correct position is:

options.A: Only the 64 letters originally written in Hindi are counted as Hindi correspondence; the translated drafts are not counted
options.B: All 160 letters are counted as Hindi correspondence, as all of them were issued in Hindi
options.C: Only the 96 translated letters are counted as Hindi correspondence
options.D: None of the letters is counted, as the office also issued letters in English draft form

e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence. The 96 letters drafted in English and translated before issue are not counted, leaving only the 64 original Hindi letters.

q: An accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 63 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:
e: Cash awards on passing Pragya are graded by marks; at 63 per cent marks the admissible award under the Hindi Teaching Scheme slab stated in the question is Rs 1,600.

q: A junior clerk passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 57 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award is admissible below 60 per cent marks

e: Cash awards on passing Pragya are graded by marks; at 57 per cent marks the admissible award under the Hindi Teaching Scheme slab stated in the question is Rs 800.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 91 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: The award is not admissible, as 95 per cent marks are required
options.B: The award is admissible only if he has also passed Hindi stenography
options.C: No cash award is admissible for the typewriting examination at any marks
options.D: The cash award is admissible, as he has secured 90 per cent or more marks

e: A cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks. With 91 per cent marks the typist satisfies that condition.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 89 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: The cash award is admissible, as he has secured 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: The award is not admissible, as 90 per cent marks are required
options.C: The award is admissible only on securing full marks
options.D: No cash award is admissible for the stenography examination

e: A cash award for the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks. With 89 per cent marks the stenographer satisfies that condition.

q: In the Hindi typewriting test conducted under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the speed recorded for a candidate is 32 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, his result is:

options.A: He has failed, as the prescribed speed is 40 words per minute
options.B: He has passed, having attained more than the prescribed speed of 30 words per minute
options.C: He has failed, as the prescribed speed is 35 words per minute
options.D: The result is withheld, speed being irrelevant to the typewriting examination

e: The prescribed Hindi typewriting speed is 30 words per minute. A recorded speed of 32 words per minute exceeds the standard, so the candidate has passed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 84 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He has failed, as the prescribed speed is 100 words per minute
options.B: He has failed, as the prescribed speed is 90 words per minute
options.C: He has passed, having attained more than the prescribed speed of 80 words per minute
options.D: He has passed only if his accuracy is also above 95 per cent

e: The prescribed Hindi stenography speed is 80 words per minute. A speed of 84 words per minute exceeds the standard, so the candidate has passed.

q: A 36-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is optional for him, training being compulsory only up to the age of 30 years
options.B: He cannot be trained, as training is imparted only to employees above 40 years
options.C: He must first pass the Prabodh examination on his own before nomination
options.D: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him, he not having attained the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee without working knowledge of Hindi who has not attained 45 years. A 36-year-old therefore must undergo the training.

q: An employee aged 50 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for him, he having attained the age of 45 years
options.B: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him up to the age of 55 years
options.C: He can be trained only through correspondence courses
options.D: He must be trained, as there is no age exemption under the Scheme

e: Compulsory in-service Hindi training applies only up to 45 years of age. An employee aged 50 years is beyond that limit, so the training is not compulsory for him.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 120, of whom 102 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as cent per cent of the staff must have working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, 85 per cent of its staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi, which is more than the prescribed 80 per cent
options.C: The office cannot be notified, as the prescribed proportion is 90 per cent
options.D: Notification is automatic and does not depend on the proportion of staff having working knowledge of Hindi

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent of staff to have working knowledge of Hindi. Here 102 of 120 is 85 per cent, which exceeds 80 per cent, so the office can be notified.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 240, of whom 180 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, as the prescribed proportion is 60 per cent
options.B: The office can be notified, as the prescribed proportion is 75 per cent
options.C: The office cannot be notified, 75 per cent of its staff having working knowledge of Hindi being below the prescribed 80 per cent
options.D: The office stands notified automatically on crossing 50 per cent

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent of staff to have working knowledge of Hindi. Here 180 of 240 is 75 per cent, below 80 per cent, so the office cannot be notified.
